legend: Well-developed cavernous blood vessels are characteristic in head and neck paragangliomas.

Small tumour cell nests composed of chief cells, which have abundant clear cytoplasm and oval-shaped nuclei with fairly low N:C ratios, are surrounded by capillaries. Capillary endothelial cells are evident.
Synaptophysin immunohistochemistry is strongly positive without exception.
GATA3 is positive in paraganglioma (in those with good tissue preservation).
Vacuolations of variable size are evident in tumour cells in SDH-related paragangliomas, such as this SDHD-deficient example from the carotid body.
SDHD-related carotid body paraganglioma. Emboli in vessels are frequently observed in operated tumour tissue consequent to marked tissue degeneration.
Staining for tyrosine hydroxylase is of variable intensity and diffuse in the tumour cell cytoplasm; stromal cells are negative.

Classic anatomical and functional imaging characteristics in a patient imaged at the age of 19 years. To exclude metastases, a 68Ga-DOTATOC PET-CT was acquired, showing bright labelling consistent with intense expression of SSTR. In this case, T2-weighted MRI showed a hypervascular tumour in the bifurcation of the carotid artery. To assess potential surgical options CT angiography was performed, further demarcating the lesion, which was deemed unresectable due to encasement of the internal and external carotid. Genetic testing showed a germline SDHD mutation.

Dr. Arthur J. A. T. Braat,

legend: The spongy cut surface of this sporadic carotid paraganglioma corresponds to cavernous blood vessels that communicated with vessels in the tumour capsule. Prominent, well-formed nests of clear tumour cells were highlighted by immunohistochemical stains for S100 and SOX10 (not shown). Note the intratumoural variation in the density of the sustentacular cells, with a gradient in this case from the periphery to the centre. A small nerve outside the tumour is present at the lower right.

Carotid body paraganglioma. Prominent, well-formed nests of tumour cells are highlighted by immunohistochemical staining for S100 (nuclear and cytoplasmic). Note the intratumoural variation in the density of sustentacular cells. A small nerve outside the tumour is present at the lower right.

The spongy cut surface of this sporadic carotid body paraganglioma corresponds to cavernous blood vessels that communicated with vessels in the tumour capsule. Prominent, well-formed nests of clear tumour cells are highlighted by SOX10 (nuclear, shown here). A small nerve outside the tumour is present at the lower right.

The relative levels of expression of neuroendocrine markers in this apparently sporadic carotid body paraganglioma are those generally seen in other head and neck parasympathetic paragangliomas. Chromogranin A can be expressed in a patchy pattern, and often in only a dot-like cytoplasmic distribution.

The relative levels of expression of neuroendocrine markers in this apparently sporadic carotid body paraganglioma are the same as those generally seen in other head and neck parasympathetic paragangliomas. Tyrosine hydroxylase (shown here) is often absent or focal.

This fibrotic SDHB-mutated carotid body paraganglioma encases the carotid artery and extends to resection margins. The tumour was removed in an en bloc resection followed by a synthetic carotid artery graft. The patient, who was 22 years old when the tumour was discovered, was found to have a germline SDHB mutation.

This fibrotic SDHB-mutated carotid body paraganglioma encased the carotid artery and extended to resection margins. Areas with a nested Zellballen pattern were present focally at the periphery of the tumour, but the tumour mostly consisted of small cells with solid and infiltrative growth. S100 immunohistochemistry showed extremely rare sustentacular cells in these areas.

This neck mass was discovered on follow-up scanning in a patient with a germline SDHB mutation who had had an ipsilateral sclerotic infiltrating paraganglioma resected 4 years earlier. The carotid body lesion was 4–8 mm in diameter and protruded from the lumen of a vein. In contrast to the initial tumour, which for the most part was highly cellular and consisted of small cells with infiltrative and solid growth patterns and extremely rare sustentacular cells, this tumour consists of relatively large cells with relatively well-formed nests and readily identified sustentacular cells. The tumour was initially suspected of being a lymph node metastasis. Because no lymph node was present, it was considered to be a local recurrence, most likely from peripheral areas of the original neoplasm. The Ki-67 proliferation index was comparable in solid areas of the initial tumour.

This neck mass was discovered on follow-up scanning in a patient with a germline SDHB mutation who had had an ipsilateral sclerotic infiltrating paraganglioma resected 4 years earlier. The lesion was 4–8 mm in diameter and protruded from the lumen of a vein. In contrast to the initial tumour, which for the most part was highly cellular and consisted of small cells with infiltrative and solid growth patterns and extremely rare sustentacular cells (shown here by S100), this tumour consists of relatively large cells with relatively well-formed nests and readily identified sustentacular cells. The tumour was initially suspected of being a lymph node metastasis. Because no lymph node was present, it was considered to be a local recurrence, most likely from peripheral areas of the original neoplasm. The Ki-67 proliferation index was comparable in solid areas of the initial tumour.
Carotid body tumour. Large blood vessels at the tumour periphery are occluded by gel beads injected preoperatively to reduce bleeding.

SDHB-deficient paraganglioma. The tumour cells show global loss of cytoplasmic granular SDHB expression, whereas the endothelial cells (internal control) show retained (normal) cytoplasmic granular expression for SDHB.
Locations of paraganglia within the head and neck region (created on BioRender.com).
This polypoid mass was identified in the middle ear, showing a well-developed nested (Zellballen) architecture and only slight nuclear variability.

Given the proximity to bone, it is not uncommon for paragangliomas of the ear to break through bone and be identified within the interstices of the adjacent mastoid or temporal bone. The chief cells still show a Zellballen nested pattern, with cells that show limited pleomorphism.
A carotid body paraganglioma in a patient with SDHB mutation.
